messages:
Priya K: @alice_m heads-up — Support: Acme reported p95/p99 spike (~3–4x) after we pushed the continuous-batcher grace-window tweak last night. Customer is seeing timeouts and slow tail for small prompts.
Alice M: on it. link to customer logs? stack?
Priya K: pastes quick summary + link to tenant dashboard — seeing p95 ~420ms -> 1.6s and p99 ~1.2s -> 4.8s after 02:00 UTC. No auth failures, but a few 504s surfaced.
Priya K: snippet of query: ```promql
avg_over_time(latency_p99{tenant="acme"}[15m]) by (route)
```
Ben S: could be hold-window increase + larger max_batch_size causing tiny requests to wait for batch fill. We saw similar in canary last month.
Alice M: @ben_s please check continuous-batcher config that rolled at 01:48 — was a global tweak to grace_window=8ms -> 20ms and max_batch_size 16 -> 32 for throughput.
Ben S: confirmed. rollout id: r-2026-04-12-01.48. Config excerpt: ```yaml
continuous_batcher:
  grace_window_ms: 20
  max_batch_size: 32
  early_flush_threshold: 0.15
```
Marco D: Customer says tail appears only for their small prompt traffic pattern (short sequences, many tiny requests). They hit p99 timeouts during morning spike.
Alice M: reproduction steps requested — @support can you provide a small cURL that repros? Also collect request size distribution.
Priya K: added repro: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":16}'
```
Priya K: perf logs show many requests stayed in holder 15–22ms then waited extra 200–400ms before dispatch — looks like head-of-line blocking in coalesce queue.
Ben S: hypothesis: increasing max_batch_size reduced flush frequency for small prompts; grace window bump amplified head wait when traffic is bursty -> long tails. Also early_flush_threshold didn't trigger for tiny inputs due to CPU scheduling jitter.
Alice M: quick mitigation options: 1) rollback grace_window to 8ms for canary tenants, 2) set per-tenant override to max_batch_size 8 for Acme, 3) enable small-request fast-path (immediate flush for <X tokens). Which is quickest?
Ben S: fastest is rollback and set per-tenant override. Fast-path needs code change and QA.
Priya K: customer wants a fix ASAP — prefer per-tenant override while you rollback global change.
Alice M: I'll roll back global change now to previous rollout r-2026-04-11-22.30, and push per-tenant override for tenant acme->max_batch_size:8. Deploy bot will post.
deploy-bot: Deploy starting: rollback r-2026-04-11-22.30 to continuous-batcher config (target: eng-platform-canary then global). ETA ~3m.
Ben S: also adding temporary metric to monitor hold_time histogram by request_size and tenant. Query: ```promql
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(batcher_hold_time_bucket[5m])) by (le, tenant))
```
Marco D: I'll ping the customer that we're rolling back and applying tenant override, ask them to validate p95/p99 over next 15m.
Alice M: rollback complete to canary, monitoring shows p99 back to ~1.1s -> 550ms for acme canary nodes. Rolling global in 2m.
Priya K: customer confirms initial improvement: p99 dropped in canary region. They still see occasional 504s during burst but much better. 
Ben S: follow-up action items: 1) add small-request fast-path flag behind feature gate (eng task), 2) add per-tenant batching knobs in control plane UI, 3) run load tests with tiny prompt distribution to ensure no regressions.
Alice M: filed eng ticket INF-4721 for fast-path + INF-4722 for UI knobs. Assigning to Ben.
Priya K: closing loop — customer happy with mitigation for now, asked for timeline for permanent fix. Marco to own.
Marco D: noted, I'll follow up in customer thread with ETA ~2 weeks for fast-path.
Alice M: thank you team. leaving notes in incident tracker. :thumbsup:
